definition: Regurgitate means to repeat information mechanically without real understanding.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word regurgitate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know regurgitate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When visitors asked follow-up questions, the new docent could only regurgitate the wall plaque, word for anxious word.

Quote shows far more understanding than regurgitate ever implies — a line repeated on purpose, with credit, because the speaker knows exactly why it fits — while regurgitate hands words back with none.
Recite goes further than quote — whole passages delivered from memory — but it stops short of regurgitate, which adds the fatal ingredient: no understanding anywhere behind the words.

Parrot means to repeat by rote imitation, the way the bird gives back sounds it cannot mean — the everyday, slightly teasing image. Regurgitate is harsher and more clinical: information swallowed whole and brought back up unchanged, with the accusation that nothing was ever understood.

Spit back is the blunt classroom phrase for handing an answer over exactly as it was given, no thought added. Regurgitate says the same thing in a formal, biting register — the word a critic or examiner uses when memorized material comes back with no understanding behind it.

For two seasons, Dario was the quiz team's secret weapon.
He could read an almanac page once and give it back intact a week later.
His coach began to worry only when the questions changed shape.
Asked to compare two treaties instead of dating them, he recited both entries in full and looked up expectantly.
His coach finally named the habit: Dario did not learn a page, he regurgitated it -- taken in whole, given back untouched, and never once put to use.
The team kept him for the buzzer rounds, but the essay events went to slower readers who could actually use what they knew.
